# Agent packet: expire reset tokens (REQ-pr1)

## The work

### REQ-pr1

`requirement · docs/records/password-reset/10-records.md:18 · revision fed403d27cbc`

A reset token expires 15 minutes after issue.

*Implements OUT-pr1.*

## Why: the outcome it serves

### OUT-pr1

`outcome · docs/records/password-reset/10-records.md:14 · revision 798de4004225`

A user who forgot their password regains access without support.

## Rules it must obey

### CON-pr1

`constraint · docs/records/password-reset/10-records.md:23 · revision b34cd7f5b559`

Tokens are single-use and stored hashed.

*Constrains REQ-pr1.*

### DEC-pr1

`decision · docs/records/password-reset/10-records.md:28 · revision 087d32273db3`

Signed, stateless tokens with a server-side revocation list: expiry is
checked from the token itself, and a used or revoked token is refused by
the list.

*Constrains REQ-pr1.*

## Related requirements

*None: this stage stands on its own.*

## Rejected alternatives: do not build these

- **OPT-pr1.** Random opaque tokens stored server-side, looked up on every use. *Passed over for DEC-pr1.*
- **OPT-pr2.** Signed tokens with no server-side state at all; a used token cannot be refused before it expires. *Passed over for DEC-pr1.*

## Consequences to respect

- **CSQ-pr1.** Every confirm reads the revocation list, so the list is on the reset path and must be available whenever resets are. An entry can be dropped once the token it revokes has expired. *Part of DEC-pr1.*

## Interfaces

### IF-pr1

`interface · docs/records/password-reset/30-architecture.md:11 · revision 4053ad7b9d3f`

`POST /password-reset` with an email address. Always answers 202, whether
or not an account has that address, and emails a link carrying a token.

### IF-pr2

`interface · docs/records/password-reset/30-architecture.md:17 · revision a5de1287db33`

`POST /password-reset/confirm` with the token and a new password. Answers
204 when the password is changed, and 410 for a token that is expired,
already used or revoked.
